overview.title: What is Glossa?
overview.p1: Glossa is an AI translation pipeline designed for scholars, philologists, and professional translators. It runs your source text through a configurable translation pass — with its own model, prompt, and optional persona — and an AI judge that audits the result against your glossary and quality criteria.
overview.p2: An AI judge then audits the final translation against your glossary and quality criteria, assigning a semantic quality label and listing specific issues with suggested fixes.
overview.step1: Paste or import your source text
overview.step2: The translation stage processes the text with your configured model and prompt
overview.step3: Optionally, a custom persona shapes the translator's voice and domain
overview.step4: AI Judge audits: quality label, issues, suggested fixes
overview.step5: You edit the candidate translation manually
overview.step6: Export in your chosen format: .txt, .md, .html, .docx, or bilingual .md
overview.p3: The translation model and provider can be chosen freely — use Gemini or DeepSeek for fast drafts, Claude or GPT-4o for nuanced literary text, or Ollama for fully local, private processing. The judge can use a different model than the translation pass.

pipeline.title: Pipeline Configuration
pipeline.intro: Pipeline settings live in the configuration panel. It appears in two ways: in Sandbox mode it is the persistent left sidebar; in Document mode it slides in as a drawer (gear icon in the header). Either way, the panel has 4 tabs — Settings, Translation, Quality Control, and Term Registry. Here's how to set up a translation run:
pipeline.configDesc: Select source and target languages from the dropdowns. Use the swap button (⇄) to quickly reverse the direction. Enable 'Auto-Segment' to split the text into paragraph-level chunks for independent processing.
pipeline.stagesDesc: Configure the provider, model, and translation instructions for the translation pass. Use the wand icon to have the AI rewrite the prompt, or save/load prompts as reusable templates with the bookmark buttons. Rolling context can be toggled to pass the tail of the previous chunk as background context.
pipeline.runDesc: In Sandbox mode: paste your text in the center panel, click 'Stage Content' to segment it, then press 'Begin Pipeline'. In Document mode: import or paste text, open it in the Document reader, then press 'Begin Pipeline' from the config drawer or the document header. Either way, each stage runs sequentially per chunk and you see tokens stream in real time. The judge runs automatically after all stages complete.
pipeline.editDesc: The 'Candidate Translation' box is fully editable. Make manual corrections, then click 'Re-Evaluate Drafts' in the audit panel to get an updated quality judgment on your edits.
pipeline.tipDesc: Use a different model for the translation pass and the judge. A fast model (Gemini Flash, DeepSeek) works well for translation, while a stronger model (GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet) excels at auditing. Ollama models are ideal for offline work or sensitive content.

features.title: Advanced Features
features.intro: This section covers the most recent additions to Glossa.
features.configDrawerDesc: The configuration panel is always available — as the left sidebar in Sandbox mode or as a slide-in drawer (gear icon, Document mode only). It has four tabs: Settings (language pair and persona), Translation (model, provider, and translation instructions for the translation pass), Quality Control (judge model, Judge Prompt, and Coherence Prompt), Term Registry (glossary management). The panel never obstructs the document in either mode.
features.documentToolsDesc: The source and translation editors now use a collapsible toolbar so the chrome disappears when you just want to read or edit raw text. Candidate translations can be validated and locked with the green check button, while the full output of any stage opens in a dedicated modal when you click its status badge in the chunk row.
features.templatesDesc: Every prompt textarea — in each stage and in both prompts of the Audit section — has save and load template buttons. Click the bookmark (+) to save the current prompt under a name; click the open book to browse and load saved templates (with search). Templates are separated by context: stage templates do not appear in the Audit section and vice versa. Saving a template with an existing name updates it automatically.
features.refineDesc: The wand icon next to each prompt sends the current text to the AI using the currently selected provider and model. Translation stages use their own stage model; the Audit section uses the shared audit model to refine both the Judge Prompt and the Coherence Prompt. The result appears immediately in the textarea — edit it freely or press Ctrl+Z to undo.
features.tokenDesc: The header displays in real time the total tokens consumed and the estimated cost for the current session, based on official pricing for each provider. Tokens are tracked separately for each stage and for the judge. The counter updates after each completed chunk.
features.sandboxDesc: The Sandbox button in the header toggles between two working modes. Sandbox is ideal for quick tests, model comparisons, and short single-text translations without chunks. Document mode activates the chunk reader, navigable index, insights panel, and advanced segmentation controls — suited for longer texts translated in multiple independent chunks.
features.exportDesc: In Document mode, an Export button (↗) appears in the header toolbar when there are completed chunks. Clicking it opens an export dialog where you choose the format (.txt, .md, .html, .docx, or bilingual .md) and, for text formats, the chunk separator. The bilingual .md export includes the original text, translation, audit quality label, and flagged issues per chunk.
features.segmentationDesc: When you import a file (.txt, .md, .docx, .pdf), Glossa opens an import preview dialog where you can fine-tune how the document is split into chunks before it enters the workspace.
features.segmentationControlsDesc: The icon bar in the dialog header provides: Auto-segment (scissors icon) — enables splitting the text into chunks by word count; Heading-aware (hash icon, Markdown only) — attaches standalone Markdown headings to the paragraph that follows, so headings are never translated in isolation. The number input sets words per chunk (default in Settings → Segmentation Defaults). The min–max range shown next to it comes from the same settings and prevents too-short or too-long chunks.
features.segmentationCardDesc: The default view shows each chunk as a card. A border colour indicates anomalies: amber means the chunk is shorter than the minimum or longer than the maximum word threshold. Expand a card to read the full text. A rotate icon appears in amber when you have manual edits pending — click it to recalculate chunks while keeping your boundary adjustments.
features.segmentationEditorDesc: Switch to the segment editor with the toggle in the top-right corner of the dialog. This view shows the entire document as a single scrollable column of paragraphs. Chunk boundaries are displayed as horizontal dividers with the chunk number. Between any two paragraphs you can: click '+' on the gap zone to add a new boundary (split the chunk at that point); click '×' on an existing boundary to remove it (merge the two adjacent chunks). Scissors icons on individual paragraphs let you split long paragraphs at their midpoint. All edits are lossless — switching back to card view preserves every manual change.
features.chunkActionsDesc: In the Index tab of the Insights panel, each unprocessed chunk shows two inline action buttons. Split divides the chunk into two halves at its midpoint — useful when a chunk is too long or contains two distinct topics. Both halves are reset to unprocessed and can be translated independently. Merge next fuses the chunk with the one immediately below it into a single larger chunk — useful when two consecutive chunks are too short or belong to the same narrative unit. Merge is only available when neither chunk has been processed yet. Both operations are instant and reversible: re-import or re-segment the document if needed.
features.personaDesc: Each project can have an optional custom persona — a free-form system prompt opener that replaces the default 'You are an expert translator specialized in X to Y translation.' opener. Set it in the Pipeline tab, in the language-pair header. When a persona is active, a badge appears and the save/load template buttons become available. Any per-stage language pair overrides are ignored while a persona is active — the persona takes full precedence. If no persona is set, the opener is generated automatically from the configured source and target languages.
features.operationsLogDesc: The Operations tab in the Insights panel records every significant event during a pipeline run. Each entry carries a scope (pipeline, stage, audit, coherence), a level (info / success / warn / error), and — where relevant — the ID of the chunk being processed. Completion entries always include the provider and model used, plus input and output token counts. Prompt entries — emitted just before each LLM call — store the full system and user prompt in a collapsible detail field so you can inspect exactly what was sent to the model. For Ollama, an 'Ollama still alive' entry appears whenever the idle timeout fires but the model is confirmed still running, indicating the model is computing a long response rather than having crashed.
features.insightsDesc: In Document mode, the Insights panel slides in from the right (panel icon in the header). It has two levels: the Document panel and the Chunk panel. The Document panel has four tabs — Index (navigable list of all chunks with inline Split / Merge actions), Stats (aggregate token usage, cost breakdown by provider and model, and word-count distribution), Coherence (cross-segment consistency audit — see Audit section), and Glossary (active dictionary terms with match status). The Chunk panel opens when you select a chunk and has three tabs — Audit (quality label, issues, suggested fixes for the selected chunk), Notes (a free-text scratchpad attached to the chunk), and Operations (the full log of every LLM call for that chunk, including prompts and token counts).
features.statsDesc: The Stats tab in the Document panel of the Insights sidebar shows aggregate metrics for the current session: total input and output tokens broken down by provider and model, estimated cost per stage and for the judge, and a per-chunk word count. Useful for tracking spend across long documents translated in multiple runs.
features.watchdogDesc: A background watchdog monitors chunks that are in the 'processing' state for longer than expected. If a chunk appears stuck — for instance when an Ollama model takes a very long time on a large context — a warning appears in the Index tab with a Cancel button to abort that specific chunk without stopping the entire pipeline.

streaming.title: Real-time Streaming
streaming.p1: All three pipeline phases — translation stages, the AI Judge, and the coherence audit — stream tokens in real time. As the model generates text you see it appear token by token, which gives immediate feedback and lets you spot issues without waiting for the full response.
streaming.p2: Streaming works across all five providers: Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, and Ollama. The connection uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) on the Rust backend, with Tauri events relaying tokens to the frontend. The judge and coherence phases stream into an internal buffer and parse the final JSON once the stream closes.
streaming.p3: If a stage fails during streaming, the system retries automatically with exponential backoff (up to 3 attempts). Timeout errors are not retried — if the model is still processing, Glossa waits rather than re-queuing the request.

audit.title: Audit & Quality Control
audit.intro: The Audit section shows quality results from the AI Judge. In Sandbox mode the right panel displays audit results; in Document mode, select a chunk and open the Chunk panel → Audit tab. After the pipeline completes, each chunk receives a semantic quality label. The judge produces five categories of issues:
audit.glossaryIssue: The translation deviates from the terms defined in your Term Registry.
audit.accuracyIssue: The meaning of the source text is not faithfully rendered in the translation.
audit.fluencyIssue: The translation reads unnaturally or has awkward phrasing in the target language.
audit.grammarIssue: Grammatical errors, incorrect conjugations, or syntactic issues in the output.
audit.consistencyIssue: Terminology or phrasing is inconsistent with other chunks in the same document.
audit.reeval: After manually editing the candidate translation, click 'Re-Evaluate Drafts' (Sandbox) or the re-audit icon on the chunk (Document mode) to run the judge again on your updated text.
audit.issuesNav: In Document mode, issue cards in the Chunk panel open the relevant chunk and scroll to the flagged text. Jumping to the exact text fragment is heuristic until the judge returns structured offsets.
audit.coherenceDesc: The coherence audit is a separate, document-level quality pass that checks cross-segment consistency — terminology stability, narrative continuity, and glossary adherence across chunk boundaries. Run it from the Coherence tab in the Insights panel (Document mode) after all chunks have been translated. It uses the Coherence Prompt from the Quality Control tab and the same shared audit model as the judge. Results appear as a list of consistency issues in the Coherence tab.

projects.title: Projects & Files
projects.intro: Glossa saves your work in local SQLite — all data stays on your machine.
projects.createDesc: You can start working immediately in an unsaved draft. When you want to persist it, click Save in the header: on the first save a lightweight dialog asks for the project name. The Projects panel remains useful for opening, explicitly creating, or deleting saved projects.
projects.saveDesc: Click the save icon at any time to persist the current state. When you reopen a project, the full pipeline config, stages, glossary, and translations are restored exactly as you left them.
projects.importExportDesc: Use the Upload icon to import a .txt, .md, .docx, or .pdf file as source text (an import preview dialog lets you fine-tune segmentation before the text enters the workspace). To export, switch to Document mode: the Export button (↗) appears in the header when chunks are completed. Clicking it opens a dialog where you pick the format (.txt, .md, .html, .docx, or bilingual .md) and the chunk separator.
projects.autosaveDesc: Glossa automatically saves the current project state in the background whenever you make changes. The save-status badge in the header shows the current state: a pencil icon for an unsaved draft, a dot for unsaved changes (dirty), a spinner while saving, and a green tick when everything is persisted. An explicit Save at any time forces an immediate write.

providers.title: LLM Providers
providers.intro: Glossa supports five providers. Each stage and the judge can use a different provider and model. Configure API keys in Settings.
providers.anthropicNote: Claude models. Excellent for nuanced, literary text.
providers.deepseekNote: Chinese AI lab. Competitive pricing, good multilingual support.
providers.ollamaNote: Runs locally. No API key. Fully private.
providers.security: API keys are stored in your operating system's keychain (GNOME Keyring on Linux, Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows). They are never written to disk in plain text and never sent anywhere except to the provider's API endpoint.

ollama.title: Using Ollama
ollama.intro: Ollama lets you run open-source LLMs entirely on your machine. No API key needed, no data leaves your computer. This is ideal for sensitive documents or offline work.
ollama.installDesc: Download from ollama.com or use the install script:
ollama.pullDesc: Download the model you want to use. Popular choices for translation:
ollama.serveDesc: Ollama must be running in the background. If it's not already:
ollama.useDesc: Open Settings — the Ollama section shows connection status and available models. Select 'ollama' as the provider in any stage or the judge, then pick a model from the dropdown.
ollama.recommendedDesc: For general translation: llama3.2 (8B), mistral (7B), or gemma2 (9B). For higher quality on a capable machine: llama3.1:70b or mixtral:8x7b. Smaller models (< 3B parameters) may produce lower quality translations.
ollama.thinkDesc: Some Ollama models support an extended reasoning step before producing their answer. In the Ollama section of Settings you can set the Think level: off (disabled), or low / medium / high for progressively deeper reasoning. A higher level can improve translation accuracy at the cost of extra time and tokens. Only enable it for models that explicitly support thinking — enabling it on standard models has no effect.

glossary.title: Library: Dictionaries & Prompt Templates
glossary.intro: Glossa includes a global library of reusable dictionaries shared across projects. Each dictionary holds source→translation pairs with optional notes. You can assign a dictionary to a project, edit its entries, and bulk-import terms from CSV files.
glossary.libraryDesc: Click the Library icon in the header (General cluster, far right) to open the panel. In the Dictionaries tab you can create new dictionaries, rename them (double-click), duplicate them (Fork), delete them, and import terms from CSV/TSV. Expand a dictionary to edit its entries inline.
glossary.csvDesc: Click the Upload button next to any dictionary to import terms from a file. A wizard shows a preview of the first 5 rows and asks for a strategy: «Add/update» adds new terms without touching existing ones; «Replace all» deletes all entries and reimports from the file. Recognised headers: term/source/from for the source term, translation/target/to for the translation (case-insensitive). The notes column is optional.
glossary.projectDesc: In the Project Configuration panel (gear icon → Registry tab) you'll find a dropdown to select the dictionary assigned to the project. Edit entries inline in the editor: changes affect the shared dictionary and are persisted with the Save button that appears as soon as you make a change. The same dictionary can be assigned to multiple projects: entries are shared, and updating an entry from one project updates it for all.
glossary.highlightDesc: In the document reader and Sandbox mode, the Highlight terms button (brush icon) in the chunk action bar activates a visual overlay. In the source text, terms present in the dictionary are underlined in blue. In the candidate translation, correctly translated terms appear with a green background; source terms found but with a missing or different translation appear with a red background. Hover over a highlighted term to see the expected translation and any notes.
glossary.auditDesc: The AI Judge specifically checks adherence to the assigned dictionary. If the translation uses a different term than what's defined in the registry, it will flag a 'glossary' issue with severity and a suggested fix. This is especially valuable for technical, legal, or academic texts where terminology must be consistent.
glossary.templatesDesc: In the Library panel (Prompt Templates tab) you manage the global collection of reusable templates. Create a template by specifying a name, context (Stage or Audit), and prompt text. Use the wand button in the creation form to have the AI rewrite the prompt: select the provider and model from the inline dropdowns and click the wand. Saved templates are available in all translation stages and in both prompts of the Audit section via the bookmark buttons (save/load).
